_note: Machine-readable NEXUS scenario contracts. Each runbook declares not only an installable agent roster but also the governing object, explicit non-object, accountable decision owner, mandatory decision/evidence artifacts, and termination criteria. The Strategic Assurance Lead is mandatory in every material runbook. Agent entries are filename-stem slugs and must resolve to catalog agents. Strategy documentation constrains orchestration; it does not grant real-world execution authority.

runbooks.title: Startup MVP Build
runbooks.summary: Test a bounded product thesis and ship the smallest evidence-generating product without confusing feature delivery with product-market validation.
runbooks.governing_object: Establish whether a specific customer problem can be solved by a usable, supportable product strongly enough to justify the next material investment.
runbooks.non_object: Maximize feature count, sprint velocity, launch speed, or demo polish as ends in themselves.
runbooks.termination_criteria: Close, redesign, or narrow the initiative when the declared falsifier is met, required authority/resources cannot be obtained, or the minimum sufficient result is achieved and transferred to ordinary ownership.

roster.activation: when permitted by the current strategic output
only after the relevant value and audience hypothesis is testable

runbooks.title: Enterprise Feature Development
runbooks.summary: Deliver a material enterprise capability without sacrificing system integrity, compliance, maintainability, or stakeholder authority for roadmap completion.
runbooks.governing_object: Produce a validated enterprise capability that improves the declared user/business outcome while remaining compatible with the existing product, controls, and operating model.
runbooks.non_object: Ship the roadmap item, maximize scope, or satisfy a single stakeholder metric regardless of system-level consequences.
runbooks.decision_owner: Authorized product/program owner with relevant security/compliance concurrence
runbooks.termination_criteria: Stop or redesign when a fatal security/compliance/architecture condition emerges, the causal benefit thesis is falsified, or the validated capability is transferred to normal product and operations ownership.

roster.activation: when permitted by the current strategic output
as required by scope and before the relevant commitment
as needed and at material gates

runbooks.title: Multi-Channel Marketing Campaign
runbooks.summary: Test and scale a coordinated market-response hypothesis while keeping channel activity subordinate to a measurable commercial or behavioral outcome.
runbooks.governing_object: Produce a defined audience behavior or commercial result through a compliant, brand-coherent campaign whose causal assumptions and measurement limits remain explicit.
runbooks.non_object: Maximize impressions, posting frequency, engagement, follower growth, or channel coverage without proving their contribution to the declared result.
runbooks.termination_criteria: Stop, reallocate, or redesign when the response hypothesis is falsified, marginal spend/effort no longer contributes to the governing object, a compliance/brand constraint is breached, or the campaign objective is reached and measurement closes.

roster.activation: when permitted by the current strategic output
only where the audience and channel hypothesis justify them

runbooks.title: Incident Response
runbooks.duration: incident-dependent; minutes to hours for containment, longer for conservation
runbooks.summary: Restore critical service safely, preserve evidence, and prevent recurrence without optimizing MTTR at the expense of integrity or learning.
runbooks.governing_object: Return the affected service to a safe, supportable condition while preserving evidence, controlling blast radius, and establishing the changes needed to prevent recurrence.
runbooks.non_object: Minimize MTTR, close the incident, or restore green dashboards regardless of residual risk, evidence loss, or recurrence.
runbooks.decision_owner: Named incident authority under the organization's incident policy
runbooks.termination_criteria: End emergency mode only when containment and recovery criteria are met, residual risks have owners, temporary authority/access is expired or transferred, and conservation actions are assigned to ordinary ownership.

roster.activation: according to the incident authority and affected system

runbooks.title: HTP Gate 0 — Solana + Arbitrum
runbooks.summary: Close an evidence-first, non-executing Gate 0 for bounded Solana and Arbitrum One DeFi risk-monitoring workstreams with chain-specific engineering, security, research, and legal review.
runbooks.governing_object: Determine whether a bounded, defensive Solana + Arbitrum One monitoring MVP is coherent, supportable, legally reviewable, and falsifiable before any live-service or executing capability is authorized.
runbooks.non_object: Maximize chain coverage, MEV capture, exploitability knowledge, detector count, or speed to live execution.
runbooks.decision_owner: HTP Governance or explicitly delegated Gate 0 owner
runbooks.termination_criteria: Gate 0 closes with PROCEED, PROCEED_WITH_CONDITIONS, REDESIGN, or REJECT once the bounded artifacts and evidence are sufficient; HOLD persists only while a named evidence/authority condition remains unresolved. No Gate 0 result authorizes live offensive or executing capability.

roster.activation: domain map, technical reconciliation, and S1 handoff
jurisdiction/activity memo and before any live-service expansion
